extracted.intended_audience: NIH K08 study section reviewers; K08 applicants and mentors (biomedical researchers preparing career-development grant applications)
extracted.subtask_description: A career-development (K08) grant proposal in biomedical research proposing systems-biology studies of malaria immunity, including candidate bio, specific aims, didactic/training plan, mentors, preliminary data, and research strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power and sample size adequacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Added simulation-based estimates of effect sizes using our proposed statistical methods and sample sizes based on the actual number of existing biological samples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justify power with simulations tailored to the planned analytic methods and the real number of available biospecimens; address reviewer concerns about sample-size limitations explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of ongoing productivity during award
rubrics_metrics.description: I am currently involved in 7 projects (5 using data previously collected ... and 2 involving new data collection). Based on our prior experience, we expect these activities to produce 4-6 publications over the next 2 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List current projects, their data sources, collaborators, and realistic publication targets to demonstrate continued scholarly output during the award period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate background and qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative of training (MSTP, PhD work on PvRBP1), field research experience, first-author publications, clinical training (Internal Medicine residency, Infectious Diseases fellowship), and prior cohort establishment and analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise but comprehensive career narrative showing relevant technical skills, prior accomplishments, leadership of studies/cohorts, and peer-reviewed publications that establish the candidate's capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear career development goals and objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Long-term goal: acquire expertise in systems biology of malaria; Short-term goals (focus of K award) include determining immune parameters predictive of clinical and sterile immunity; Career objectives: Objective 1 (advance knowledge in biostatistics/computational biology) and Objective 2 (elucidate mechanisms of immunity using experiments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State explicit, measurable short- and long-term career goals tied to the proposed training and research; define concrete objectives (e.g., skills to be acquired and research milestones).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentoring plan with named mentors and commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: Assembled interdisciplinary mentors (Dr. Chandy C. John – primary mentor; Dr. Wanzhu Tu, Dr. Lang Li, Dr. Peter D. Crompton – co-mentors) with mentoring histories, relevant expertise, and specified meeting frequencies (biweekly, monthly, monthly teleconferences & 2 conferences/year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name mentors, summarize their expertise/funding/mentoring record, and specify frequency and modes of meetings plus documented access to resources and data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structured didactic training curriculum
rubrics_metrics.description: Didactic training includes immunology (AAI Advanced Course), epidemiology (PBHL E517, E601), advanced biostatistics (B670 family, B642), bioinformatics/computational biology courses (INFO series), Coursera 'Systems Biology Specialization', and a Cold Spring Harbor course on statistical methods for functional genomics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List specific courses (with course codes when applicable), credit hours or expected weekly commitment, modality (in-person/online), and map each to the skills they will develop.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protected research effort
rubrics_metrics.description: My effort for the K08 will be 20% clinical and 80% dedicated to research and career development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State percent effort devoted to research and justify that it is sufficient to complete the proposed training and research aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional support and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: IUSM provided a generous three-year start-up package including funding for equipment and a technician, independent lab and office space, and 80% protected research time to facilitate development as an independent scientist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document start-up funds, space, personnel support, and institutional commitments that enable successful execution of the project and career development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to biospecimens and clinical data
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentors Dr. Crompton and Dr. Traore have kindly agreed to allow me access to biospecimens and clinical data from their clinical study for this grant proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify the types/quantity of specimens and datasets available, permission agreements, and how access supports the research aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims: testable hypotheses and measurable outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific Aim 1: Identify immune parameters predictive of clinical and sterile immunity using transcriptomics, multiplex cytokine analysis, Pf-specific antibody profiling, flow cytometry, and modeling; Specific Aim 2: Compare profiles between immune classes and relate to in vitro parasite-inhibitory activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present 2–4 concise, hypothesis-driven aims with clear outcome measures, planned assays, and analytic approaches that map to the hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance: public health relevance and knowledge gap
rubrics_metrics.description: Malaria afflicts ~200 million people annually; current vaccines (e.g., RTS,S) have limited efficacy in target populations, and unambiguous immune correlates of protection are lacking; understanding mechanisms of clinical and sterile immunity will inform vaccine design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame the problem's magnitude, articulate the knowledge gap, and explain how the proposed work will advance the field or impact public health.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation: novel methods and unique cohort/resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Innovation lies in longitudinal biospecimens linked to >3 years of prospective clinical data, unbiased systems-biology approaches, and identification of a subset of children apparently protected from BSI despite exposure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight novel conceptual or methodological elements, unique datasets/resources, or new paradigms that differ from current approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach: rigorous methods and research strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: General strategy to analyze baseline biospecimens from immune/susceptible children using global analyses of host immune factors, machine learning and statistical models, complementary functional experiments, and re-interrogation for occult infection when needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a logical, detailed plan linking hypotheses to experiments/analyses, address potential pitfalls and alternative strategies, and justify chosen methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary data demonstrating feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary data showed baseline whole-blood gene expression differences between clinically immune and susceptible children, higher Pf-specific antibody levels in clinically immune children, and a subset of children with no detectable BSI but evidence of exposure via antibody boosting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include quantitative preliminary results (figures, p/FDR values) that establish feasibility and justify the proposed studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome definitions and measurement methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Children defined as clinically immune or susceptible based on 3 years of surveillance; sterile immunity operationalized as remaining free of BSI by bi-weekly PCR throughout a 6-month high-transmission season plus evidence of exposure by antibody boosting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear, operational definitions for primary outcomes and describe surveillance/assay schedules (e.g., bi-weekly PCR), including thresholds and confirmatory measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical and computational analysis plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of machine learning algorithms and statistical models (e.g., generalized linear models, edgeR for RNA-seq), pathway/upstream regulator analysis, and multiple-testing control (FDR <5%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify software/packages, analytic pipelines, feature-selection strategies, cross-validation, handling of confounders, and multiple-comparison corrections appropriate to -omics data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan to detect occult (ultrasensitive) infections
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-interrogate for occult BSI using a recently developed ultrasensitive quantitative real-time PCR (qPCR) assay that improves sensitivity by as much as 30-fold relative to the original PCR assay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate higher-sensitivity assays when necessary to resolve alternative hypotheses about occult infection driving immune signatures; detail assay performance and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline and milestones with percent effort
rubrics_metrics.description: Timeline table mapping years 1–5 to workshops, courses, online specialization, CITI, grant-writing, and conference attendance with percent effort/year where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a year-by-year schedule of training and research milestones, indicating percent effort and expected timing for deliverables (e.g., manuscript submissions, course completion, R01 submission).

rubrics_metrics.name: Training in research ethics and grantsmanship/writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Planned training includes Introduction to Research Ethics (GRAD G504), Responsible Conduct of Research and CITI renewals, Grant Writer’s Workshop & Scientific Writing Course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include required ethics training and targeted grantsmanship/writing courses to strengthen independence and future funding applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan for dissemination and next-stage funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Four collaborative projects will be finalized this year with manuscripts submitted for publication prior to the start of the current proposal; plan to submit first R01 application in years 4 and 5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe publication goals and concrete plans for advancing to independent funding (R01 submission timeline) and how K-era work will enable that transition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular communication and collaboration mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Meeting schedule includes biweekly individual meetings with primary mentor, monthly meetings with co-mentors for biostatistics/modeling and computational guidance, monthly teleconferences and in-person research discussions at 2 conferences per year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document frequency and format of mentor-mentee interactions and collaborative team meetings to ensure oversight and progress monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility via well-characterized longitudinal cohort
rubrics_metrics.description: Ongoing cohort in Kalifabougou, Mali with bi-weekly active surveillance, archived DBS/plasma/whole-blood RNA/PBMCs and >3 years of linked clinical, parasitological, and epidemiologic data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide cohort retention, sample collection schedules, data linkage, and evidence that sample types/volumes are sufficient for planned assays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsiveness to reviewer critiques and proposal revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Revisions include better characterized immune and susceptible class definitions, more thorough description of computational methods, and more rigorous statistical didactic regime resulting from reviewers' suggestions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly address reviewer concerns in resubmissions by revising definitions, expanding methodological detail, strengthening training plans, and documenting how changes improve study power/rigor.
